title: Coefficient construction and surjectivity for a completed monomial chart
statement:
Let $(A,\mathfrak m)$ be a nonzero Noetherian local commutative ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], $k=A/\mathfrak m$, and $P$ a fine saturated sharp additive monoid [def-trf-fs-log-blowup]; sharp means that $0$ is its only invertible element. Let $a:(P,+)	o(A,\cdot)$ be a monoid homomorphism with $a(q)\in\mathfrak m$ for every $q
e0$, and put $I=(a(q):q
e0)A$. Suppose $R=A/I$ is regular local [def-weil-regular-scheme], let $n=\dim R$, and choose lifts $u_1,\ldots,u_n\in A$ of a regular system of parameters of $R$ [def-weil-pbc-regular-system-of-parameters]. Put $S=\widehat A=\varprojlim_j A/\mathfrak m^j$ [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion], and write $\widehat a(q),\widehat u_i$ for the canonical images in $S$. Then $\mathfrak m=I+(u_1,\ldots,u_n)$, and $S$ is a complete Noetherian local ring with maximal ideal $\mathfrak mS$, residue field $k$, and $\dim S=\dim A$ [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring]. There exist a coefficient ring $L$ and a homomorphism $\lambda:L	o S$ inducing an isomorphism on residue fields as follows: if $A$ contains a field, one can take $L=k$ and $\lambda$ a section of $S	o k$; if $A$ contains no field, $k$ has prime characteristic $p$ and one can take a Cohen ring $L=C$ with $C/pC\cong k$ [def-weil-pbc-cohen-ring]. Write $E=L[P][T_1,\ldots,T_n]$ for the ring of finite sums $cz^qT^e$, with multiplication $z^qz^{q'}=z^{q+q'}$, and $\mathfrak a=(\mathfrak m_L,z^q\ (q
e0),T_1,\ldots,T_n)$, where $\mathfrak m_k=0$ and $\mathfrak m_C=pC$. The map $E	o S$, $cz^qT^e\mapsto\lambda(c)\widehat a(q)\widehat u^e$, extends to a continuous surjective local homomorphism $\phi:B=\varprojlim_j E/\mathfrak a^j	o S$. It satisfies $\phi(z^q)=\widehat a(q)$ and $\phi(T_i)=\widehat u_i$. Moreover $B$ is $\mathfrak aB$-adically complete, $\phi(\mathfrak aB)=\mathfrak mS$, and $\phi(J)=\mathfrak mS$ for $J=(z^q\ (q
e0),T_1,\ldots,T_n)B$. The assertions include $P=\{0\}$ and $n=0$.

proof.text: The images of the $u_i$ generate the maximal ideal $\mathfrak m/I$ of $R$ by [def-weil-pbc-regular-system-of-parameters]. Thus every $x\in\mathfrak m$ differs from an $A$-linear combination of the $u_i$ by an element of $I$. Conversely $I$ and every $u_i$ lie in $\mathfrak m$. Hence $\mathfrak m=I+(u_1,\ldots,u_n)$.

source.place: Tag 00KU, definition-regular-local: parameters generate the maximal ideal; quotient-ideal calculation

proof.text: Since $A$ is Noetherian, $\mathfrak m$ is finitely generated [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-adic-completion-mod-ideal] to $(A,\mathfrak m)$: $S$ is $\mathfrak mS$-adically complete and its first-coordinate map identifies $S/\mathfrak mS$ with $k$. By [lem-weil-pbc-adic-completion-noetherian] and [lem-weil-pbc-local-completion-local-ring], $S$ is Noetherian local with maximal ideal $\mathfrak mS$. It is nonzero because its residue field is $k$. Finally [lem-weil-pbc-completion-dimension] gives $\dim S=\dim A$.

source.place: Tags 05GG lemma-hathat-finitely-generated, 0316 lemma-completion-Noetherian-Noetherian, 05GI lemma-radical-completion; dimension: more-algebra.tex Tag 07NV lemma-completion-dimension

proof.text: Suppose $A$ contains a field. Its composite map to the nonzero ring $S$ is injective, since a unital map from a field to a nonzero ring has zero kernel. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-cohen-coefficient-ring-exists] to $S$, obtaining a subring $\Lambda$ with $\Lambda\cap\mathfrak mS=p\Lambda$ and residue field $k$, where $p=\operatorname{char}k$. If $p=0$, this intersection is zero by that node. If $p>0$, the field contained in $S$ has characteristic $p$: its unital map to $k$ is injective. Thus $pS=0$, so again $\Lambda\cap\mathfrak mS=p\Lambda=0$. The stated residue isomorphism is now $\Lambda\xrightarrow{\sim}k$ itself. Its inverse followed by inclusion defines $\lambda:k\to S$, a section of $S\to k$. Set $L=k$.

source.place: Tag 032A theorem-cohen-structure-theorem (1); Tag 0326 definition-coefficient-ring and following remarks, case (1)

proof.text: Suppose $A$ contains no field. If $\operatorname{char}k=0$, every positive integer has nonzero residue and hence is a unit in $A$; the prime-ring map therefore extends to a unital injection $\mathbf Q\to A$, a contradiction. Consequently $\operatorname{char}k=p$ for a prime $p$. Choose a Cohen ring $C$ and $e:C/pC\xrightarrow{\sim}k$ using [lem-weil-pbc-cohen-rings-exist]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-cohen-ring-lift-complete-local] to the complete local ring $S$ and this residue isomorphism. It gives $\lambda:C\to S$ reducing to $e$. Set $L=C$. This does not require $A$ to be a domain or $\lambda$ to be injective; it includes rings where a power of $p$ vanishes.

source.place: Tag 0328 lemma-cohen-rings-exist; Tag 032A theorem-cohen-structure-theorem, positive-residue-characteristic construction

proof.text: Choose finitely many nonzero generators $q_1,\ldots,q_r$ for $P$, deleting $0$ from a finite generating list [def-trf-fs-log-blowup]. Every $q\ne0$ is a nonempty sum of these generators, so $z^q$ is divisible by some $z^{q_i}$. Therefore $\mathfrak a=(\mathfrak m_L,z^{q_1},\ldots,z^{q_r},T_1,\ldots,T_n)$ is finitely generated: $\mathfrak m_L$ is zero or $(p)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-adic-completion-mod-ideal], $B$ is $\mathfrak aB$-adically complete and $B/\mathfrak aB\cong E/\mathfrak a$. Sharpness implies a sum involving a nonzero element cannot equal $0$: if $q+q'=0$, $q$ is invertible. Consequently the constant-coefficient map sending every nonzero monomial and every $T_i$ to zero is a ring map $E\to L/\mathfrak m_L$ with kernel $\mathfrak a$. Thus $E/\mathfrak a\cong k$.

source.place: Tag 05GG lemma-hathat-finitely-generated; finite generators and constant-coefficient quotient of the displayed Expose VI 1.6 model

proof.text: Define $f:E\to S$ by finite-sum evaluation $cz^qT^e\mapsto\lambda(c)\widehat a(q)\widehat u^e$. Additivity is termwise; multiplicativity follows from $a(q+q')=a(q)a(q')$ and commutativity. The generators of $\mathfrak a$ map into $\mathfrak mS$, so $f(\mathfrak a^j)\subseteq(\mathfrak mS)^j$. There are therefore compatible quotient maps $f_j:E/\mathfrak a^j\to S/(\mathfrak mS)^j$. For $b=(b_j)_j\in B$, the sequence $(f_j(b_j))_j$ is compatible. Completeness of $S$ identifies it with a unique element $\phi(b)\in S$ [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion, lem-weil-pbc-adic-completion-mod-ideal]. Componentwise ring operations prove that $\phi$ is a ring map and restricts to $f$. In particular it has the prescribed values on $z^q$ and $T_i$. Since $\phi(\mathfrak aB)\subseteq\mathfrak mS$, it carries $(\mathfrak aB)^j$ into $(\mathfrak mS)^j$ and is continuous.

source.place: Tag 0317 definition-complete and Tag 05GG lemma-hathat-finitely-generated; direct componentwise inverse-limit construction

proof.text: The reduction of $\phi$ modulo $\mathfrak mS$ is exactly $B\to B/\mathfrak aB\cong L/\mathfrak m_L\xrightarrow{\sim}k$. Hence $\phi^{-1}(\mathfrak mS)=\mathfrak aB$. To check that $B$ is local, take $b\notin\mathfrak aB$. Its first coordinate is nonzero in the field $E/\mathfrak a$. For each $j$, lift the inverse of this coordinate to $E/\mathfrak a^j$; the product with $b_j$ is $1+h$ with $h\in\mathfrak a/\mathfrak a^j$ and $h^j=0$. The finite series $\sum_{i=0}^{j-1}(-h)^i$ corrects the lift to an inverse of $b_j$. These inverses are unique and commute with reduction. They form an inverse to $b$ in $B$. Since $\mathfrak aB$ is maximal, its complement consists of units and it is the unique maximal ideal. Thus $\phi$ is local.

source.place: Tag 05GI lemma-radical-completion, proof (coordinate inverses); geometric-series argument written out

proof.text: Write $\phi_*(H)$ for the ideal of $S$ generated by images of an ideal $H\subseteq B$, without yet asserting equality with the set image. Step 1 gives $\phi_*(J)=\mathfrak mS$, since the displayed generators map to $\widehat a(q)$ and $\widehat u_i$. As $J\subseteq\mathfrak aB$ and $\lambda(\mathfrak m_L)\subseteq\mathfrak mS$, also $\phi_*(\mathfrak aB)=\mathfrak mS$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-complete-source-surjective-mod-ideal] with source $B$, ideal $\mathfrak aB$ and target $S$. The source is precomplete by Step 5, the target is Hausdorff for the image ideal $\mathfrak mS$ by Step 2, and the composite $B\to S/\mathfrak mS=k$ is surjective because its restriction to $L$ is. Therefore $\phi$ is surjective. For a surjective ring map the set image of an ideal is an ideal: in a finite sum $\sum s_i\phi(h_i)$ lift each $s_i$ to $b_i\in B$, obtaining $\phi(\sum b_ih_i)$. Thus $\phi(J)=\phi(\mathfrak aB)=\mathfrak mS$, as claimed.

source.place: Tag 0315 lemma-completion-generalities, lifting method; Mathlib/RingTheory/AdicCompletion/Functoriality.lean, surjective_of_mk_map_comp_surjective, lines 447-459

proof.text: The arguments allow $P=\{0\}$: the list $q_i$ is empty and $I=0$. They also allow $n=0$, when Step 1 says $\mathfrak m=I$. If both hold, $\mathfrak m=0$, $A=k$ is a field, $S=k$, $E=B=k$, and $\phi$ is the identity with both ideals zero. In the no-field case the combination $P=\{0\},n=0$ cannot occur, since it would force $A$ to be a field. No other step used a nonempty generating list.

Checks by step: S1 m=I+(u) follows from regular-system-of-parameters (m/I generated by the u_i). S2: S is complete, Noetherian and local with maximal ideal mS, residue field k and dim S=dim A. S3: coefficient-ring clause (3) plus char F=p gives pS=0, so Lambda=k. S4: char k=0 would put Q inside A, so k has prime characteristic and the Cohen-lift hypotheses hold, with no injectivity of C->S needed. S5: the augmentation ideal is finitely generated, and sharpness makes the constant-term map multiplicative with kernel the augmentation ideal, so E/a=k. S6: f maps a into mS (lambda(p) in mS), giving compatible f_j and a limit map phi into the complete S. S7: inverses built level by level with geometric series make B local and phi local. S8: the complete-source surjectivity hypotheses all hold (B precomplete, S Hausdorff for mS, B->k onto on L), and images of ideals under a surjection are ideals, so phi(J)=phi(aB)=mS. S9: P={0} and n=0 each checked, together giving the identity of k; also checked Z_p, Z/p^2, k[[x]] and a(1)=0.
